definition: Dissonance means a lack of harmony or agreement; a clashing quality in sounds, ideas, or values.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word dissonance. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know dissonance should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The music students winced at the dissonance when both pianos struck clashing chords at the same moment.
A mismatch is a mild difference between things, while dissonance is a genuine clash that feels uncomfortable to hear or think about.
Cacophony is stronger than dissonance; dissonance is a clash between elements, while cacophony is a whole wall of harsh, jumbled noise.

Discord is open disagreement or strife, usually between people - a family or committee in discord is quarreling. Dissonance is the clashing quality itself, and it needs no quarrel: two chords, or your own values and actions, can produce dissonance with nobody arguing at all.

A clash is the collision moment itself - two colors, two egos, two schedules meeting head-on - and the word is blunt and everyday. Dissonance is the more formal, sustained lack of harmony that hangs in the air afterward: not the bang of the collision but the ongoing off-key quality it leaves.

Friction is the heat of people rubbing against each other - irritation and tension building between coworkers or allies. Dissonance is cooler and more abstract: a lack of fit between sounds, ideas, or values. Friction needs people in contact; dissonance can sit inside one mind, between belief and behavior.

Tomas prided himself on honesty, yet at his new sales job he found himself repeating small exaggerations from the official script.
The dissonance between his personal values and his daily work left him uneasy every evening.
Eventually he asked to rewrite the script so that he could believe every word he said.
This shows dissonance beyond music: the clash between what Tomas believes and what he actually does creates an uncomfortable inner conflict, which is exactly the kind of disagreement the noun names.

Dissonance is always a noun: you hear dissonance in clashing chords, feel cognitive dissonance when your actions contradict your beliefs, and notice dissonance between two policies.
The adjective form, discordant, describes something that itself lacks harmony; keep dissonance for naming the clash itself.

Marcus kept a compost bin, biked to work in the rain, and lectured his roommates about the energy cost of long showers.
He also flew home every long weekend, a habit that burned more carbon in a month than his showers could save in a decade.
For a long time he simply never put the two facts side by side.
When a classmate finally did the math out loud at dinner, Marcus felt the dissonance land almost physically -- his values and his boarding passes refusing to sit in the same key.
There was no one to argue with; the two halves of his own life were simply out of tune, and they hummed at him for weeks.
